settings.label: Performance readout in the top left: frames a second, the game's and the renderer's CPU time, the GPU's
AI missions' PF map: rooms shown black on green (the game's is black on black)
How far out rocks and shrubs are shown, x the game's (1: the game's own; more draws)
How far you see, x the game's view distance - the far land and mountains fading into the sky by true distance, no popping as you turn (1: the game's own; more draws)
Far Scenery: show buildings, trees and rocks farther away (more draws; move to refresh)
Scenery distance: up to 3x for buildings/trees, 2x for rocks/shrubs, within loaded areas
Fullness: retain more distant building and tree groups
Distant detail saving (0 full, 1 balanced shading)
Immersive Ships: brighter navigation markings and clearer distant hulls; buildings and trees reach up to 15% farther within loaded areas
Darkness: how dark nights, storms and dim places get (0 lightest, as the blue hour after sunset; 1 ao-vk's earlier nights; 2 very dark)
Day/Night Cycle: Server / Longer Day, Shorter Night / Enhanced Daylights (happier) / PermaDay / PermaNight
Depth: textures with a height map (_h.png) stand out of the surface up close (0 = flat)
Depth detail: how finely the depth is traced (more: sharper edges at flat views, slower)
World surface artwork: AnarchyHD / Enhanced Original
Distant terrain: broad rock/soil variation and slope definition
Terrain: Original / Shared Ground / Shared Ground+ (native terrain, classic lighting, no ripples; GroundOn overrides)
Surface roughness: bumps and grit in Shared Ground+ (0 smooth, 1 previous detail)
Window interiors: Off / Medium (Subtle) / Maximum (Strong) (experimental, global exterior windows)
Window lights: slow apartment activity (off uses static light states)
Building Weathering: Off / Low / Medium / High
Enhanced ground renderer (overrides Shared Ground and Shared Ground+)
ICC Tiles (off retains HD Ground artwork)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: valleys and the feet of cliffs darker, as less of the sky reaches them (0 = none)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: slopes lit from where the sun is now, not where it was when the hour's light was made (0 = as made)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: rocks and scree at the feet of cliffs and on rough slopes (0 = none, 2 = twice as many)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: small loose stones on flat dirt, gravel and sand near you (0 = none, 2 = twice as many)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: wind ripples in loose sand, in depth up close (0 = none)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: footprints in loose sand, where characters walk (0 = none)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: how deep the sand ripples are up close (0 = flat; its own, not Depth's)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: the sand ripples smoother - less wobble in their crests, less of the tile's bumps (0 = rough)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: dunes of loose sand shaped by the sun as it stands, their far sides in shade (0 = the game's flat light)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: a sparkle of sunlit grains in loose sand near you (0 = none)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: fine grit in the ground at your feet, where its texture is a soft smear (0 = none)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: neighbouring ground textures blend into each other along a ragged edge instead of meeting in a hard straight line (0 = hard edges)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: hills and cliff edges rounded, finer triangles up close (0 = the game's shapes)
Ground drawn by ao-vk: cliffs' rock stands out of their faces up close (units; 0 = flat)
Ground past that: texture detail (texels a 4 x 4 cell; 8 = the game's, 32 costs a lot of memory)
Ground drawn at full quality this many times further out (1 = the game's; above 2 the game stutters as you move)
Cliffs: the ground's texture laid on their faces, not stretched down them
Cliffs: rock laid on their faces, in the colour of the ground
Cliffs: the same tile not repeated in rows down their faces
Large patches of lighter and darker ground over the land
Soft leaf edges dithered (one pass, the TAA smooths them) from this distance (0 never)
Weather: Automatic / Clear / Overcast / Rain / Thunderstorm
Selected weather: rain or thunderstorm strength
Fog: Automatic / Halloween (black) / Mist / Custom colour
Selected fog: visibility distance in metres (Halloween reference: about 30)
Selected fog: clear distance around the camera in metres
Selected fog: dim nearby scenery (0 keeps its normal brightness; Mist ignores this)
Selected fog: softly drifting patches (0 is still)
Selected fog: apply indoors too (normally outdoors only)
Thunderstorms: how thick and dark their clouds (1: shapes and light in them; 2: one dark mass)
Heat lightning: on some warm, dry nights silent flashes in far-off clouds (x; 0: none)
Force a sandstorm (1 = full storm; 0 = the game's weather)
Sky: our own sky in place of the game's - blue by day, sunsets, the blue hour and night from the sun's height (off: the game's sky)
Sky: how much of each zone's own sky colour is kept (0: none, 1: mostly the zone's)
Sky: our sky's brightness against the game's (and the far haze's, which takes its colour)
Sky: sunrise and sunset colours - orange and red towards the sun, pink above, the pink band opposite (0: the game's sky; above 1 more vivid)
Sky: the blue hour after sunset and before sunrise - a deep blue sky going over to the night's (0: none)
Sky: the glow round the sun and along the horizon under it (0: none)
Clouds: how strongly they take the sunset's colours - gold, orange, red, pink undersides after the sun has set (0: the game's hues)
Sky: the stars come out slowly as the sky darkens after sunset, and fade before sunrise (off: as the game shows them)
Sky: our own stars - thousands, in their colours, wheeling through the night, twinkling low (0: the game's)
Sky: the galaxy's band across the night sky, x (0 none)
Sky: shooting stars on clear nights, how often x (0 none)
Sky: auroras on some clear nights, how often and how strong x (0 none)
Sky: an aurora every night, this strong (0: only some nights, by chance)
Sky: rainbows after rain, with the sun low behind you, x (0 none)
Clouds: thin high wisps, most on clear days - pink and gold round sunrise and sunset (0: none; off by default: under our own sky they showed as coarse streaks)
Clouds: quality - less noise, more cost (0 low .. 3 ultra)
Clouds: how fast they churn and change shape, x (0 still)
Contact shadows (small sun shadows the map misses)
Area lighting: daylight colour and ground bounce
Distant sky traffic: Off / Light / Busy
Wide haze round its core (0 = even; wider in rain by night)
Bright coloured lights keep their colour (0 = they go white)
Highlight glare reduction (keeps bright walls and ground gentler)
Brighter daylight look (lighter shadows, less sunset tint)
Indirect light (bounce light from the lit scene)
Sunset rays: beams fanning from a low sun through the clouds and over the hills (0: none)
Deserts: dusty air in fair weather - far dunes paler and warmer, a pale band along the horizon (0 = none)
Deserts: heat shimmer over distant land in the midday sun (0 = none)
Sun brightness (0 = the game's own sun)
Fog banks: thick mist drifting through the low ground at dawn and after rain, most in wet country (x; 0: none)
Low sun's light: golden on what faces it, the shade cooler, round sunrise and sunset (0: the game's colours)
Morning haze: the air thicker round sunrise, half as much round sunset (0: none)
Render scale: the 3D world drawn at this % of the screen's size, the TAA bringing it up to full size (lower is faster)
Experimental frame generation (AMD FSR 3.1): adds intermediate frames; may add latency
Upscaler for the render scale (0: ao-vk's own TAA, 1: AMD FSR 2.2, 2: AMD FSR 3.1)
FXAA: fast anti-aliasing, used when TAA is off (no smearing, a little softer)
Vivid Tone: contrast depth (gamma, not display HDR)
Golden hour: round sunrise and sunset the light warmer, the shade a little cooler, a touch more contrast
Neon nights: teal shadows, lights keep their colour (in place of randy-vk-night.cube)
Blur in front of the focus
